drivingQuestion: What is the scriptural source that one waits an hour before prayer (and after it)?
outcomeNote: The source for waiting before prayer is given by R' Yehoshua ben Levi and corroborated by a baraita; the difficulty about the early pious's nine daily hours is answered by their piety.

segments.he: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, אָמַר קְרָא: ״אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ״.
segments.en: The Gemara asks: «From where are these matters» derived? «Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:» This is alluded to when «the verse states: “Happy are those who dwell in Your House”» (Psalms 84:5), immediately after which it is said: “They will yet praise You, Selah.”

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל צָרִיךְ לִשְׁהוֹת שָׁעָה אַחַת אַחַר תְּפִלָּתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַךְ צַדִּיקִים יוֹדוּ לִשְׁמֶךָ יֵשְׁבוּ יְשָׁרִים אֶת פָּנֶיךָ״.
segments.en: «And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said: One who prays must» also «wait one hour after his prayer, as it is stated: “Surely the righteous will give thanks unto Your name, the upright will sit before You”» (Psalms 140:14), meaning that after thanking God through prayer, one should stay and sit before Him.

segments.he: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶא שָׁעָה אַחַת קוֹדֶם תְּפִלָּתוֹ, וְשָׁעָה אַחַת אַחַר תְּפִלָּתוֹ. קוֹדֶם תְּפִלָּתוֹ, מִנַּיִן? שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַשְׁרֵי יוֹשְׁבֵי בֵיתֶךָ״. לְאַחַר תְּפִלָּתוֹ מִנַּיִן? — דִּכְתִיב: ״אַךְ צַדִּיקִים יוֹדוּ לִשְׁמֶךָ יֵשְׁבוּ יְשָׁרִים אֶת פָּנֶיךָ״.
segments.en: «That» opinion «was also taught» in a baraita: «One who prays must wait one hour before his prayer and one hour after his prayer. From where» is it derived that one must wait one hour «before his prayer? As it is stated: “Happy are those who dwell in Your House.” And from where» is it derived that one must stay one hour «after his prayer? As it is written: “Surely the righteous will give thanks unto Your name, the upright will sit before You.”»

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ שׁוֹהִין שָׁעָה אַחַת, וּמִתְפַּלְּלִין שָׁעָה אַחַת, וְחוֹזְרִין וְשׁוֹהִין שָׁעָה אַחַת. וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁשּׁוֹהִין תֵּשַׁע שָׁעוֹת בַּיּוֹם בִּתְפִלָּה, תּוֹרָתָן הֵיאַךְ מִשְׁתַּמֶּרֶת, וּמְלַאכְתָּם הֵיאַךְ נַעֲשֵׂית?
segments.en: «The Sages taught» in a baraita with regard to waiting before and after prayer: «The early» generations of «pious» men «would wait one hour, pray one hour, then wait one hour again.» This raises the question: «Since» the early pious men «would spend nine hours per day» engaged either «in prayer» or the requisite waiting periods before and after prayer, three hours each for the morning, afternoon, and evening prayers, «how is their Torah preserved?» There was little time remaining to review their studies. «And how was their work accomplished?»

segments.he: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁחֲסִידִים הֵם — תּוֹרָתָם מִשְׁתַּמֶּרֶת, וּמְלַאכְתָּן מִתְבָּרֶכֶת.
segments.en: The Gemara answers: «Rather, because they were pious» they merited that «their Torah is preserved and their work is blessed.»
